blocks.text: Managing Chrome profiles for support tasks

Support staff often manage multiple accounts for different clients or internal systems. Using separate Chrome profiles is the best way to keep these environments isolated. Go to the Profile icon in the top right corner and click Add. This keeps your bookmarks, passwords, and history clean for each specific project or client.

When users report that a site is not loading, start by checking their cache. You can clear browsing data by pressing ⌘ + ⇧ + Delete. If the issue is site-specific, use the developer tools to inspect network activity. Press ⌥ + ⌘ + I to open these tools. Look at the Network tab to see if any requests are failing with a 404 or 500 error.

Lazur helps you handle the administrative load of support work. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask where a specific setting is, and Lazur will circle it on your screen. Use the dictation feature by holding the fn key to write your ticket resolutions faster. This reduces the time spent typing out repetitive instructions for common issues.

items: ⌘ + T: Open a new tab for a new ticket research task.
⌘ + L: Jump directly to the address bar to enter a URL or search query.
⌘ + ⇧ + T: Reopen the last closed tab if you accidentally close a ticket page.
⌘ + 1 to 8: Switch between your primary support tabs quickly.
⌘ + Option + Right Arrow: Move to the next tab in your current window.

blocks.text: Too many extensions slow down your browser and consume memory. Periodically review your installed extensions by typing chrome://extensions in the address bar. Disable or remove anything you do not use daily. If you need a specific tool for a task, install it and pin it to the toolbar for quick access.

Writing documentation is a major part of your day. Use Lazur to dictate your findings while you have the browser open. This keeps your hands on the keyboard for other tasks. If you need to find a specific article in your knowledge base, use the search bar and ask Lazur to point at the best result if you get stuck.

Sometimes you need to block third party cookies or manage site permissions for specific users. Navigate to Chrome > Settings > Privacy and security. Here you can control site settings and manage how cookies are handled. For specific sites, click the icon to the left of the URL to see permissions like camera, microphone, and notifications.

faq.question: How do I clear site data for just one website?
faq.answer: Click the icon to the left of the URL in the address bar, then select Site settings. From there, you can clear data for that specific site without affecting your entire browser history.

faq.question: Can Lazur help me with Chrome settings?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where a setting is. It will draw a circle around the correct menu item on your screen.

faq.question: Is Chrome the best browser for IT support on Mac?
faq.answer: Chrome is highly effective due to its developer tools and extension ecosystem, which are standard for most web-based support platforms.
